transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too, Doc. Well, I guess what brings me in is that... ever since I stopped working, I just can't seem to slow down. I'm up and moving from one little job to the next all day long. It's like I still have a crew waiting on me or something, and I just can't turn it off.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or excited for you?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not running around because I'm thrilled about something. I don't get these big bursts of excitement or anything like that. It's just... I can't sit still. It's not a mood thing, it's just this feeling like I have to be doing something.
Do unwanted thoughts keep popping into your mind and make you feel like you have to stay busy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't get, you know, strange thoughts or worries stuck in my head. It's not my mind telling me I have to do things to get rid of a thought... it's really just my body. I just feel restless if I'm not moving around and doing something, but there's no specific thought driving it.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?

No, I don't really worry all that much. I mean, everyday things are just... everyday things. I don't sit around stressing over bills or what's going to happen tomorrow. Like I said, it's more just this physical need to be moving, not that I'm anxious or worried about anything in particular.
When you were a child, were you also the kind of person who had a hard time sitting still?

Yeah, I was. I mean, even back in grade school, my teachers used to say I was bright but... scattered, I guess. I was always losing my pencils, or I'd just call out answers without waiting my turn. And they always had to give me reminders to actually finish my work before I could go out for recess. So, yeah, it's really been like this my whole life.

latest_inference.note: Lifelong history since childhood of hyperactivity/impulsivity and inattention (couldn't sit still, losing things, blurting out answers, needing reminders to finish work) strongly supports ADHD. Denial of elevated mood, intrusive thoughts/compulsions, and generalized worry makes prior alternatives less likely, so F41.1 and F43.8 are ruled out.
